findings.title: Java ChoiceFormat / single-brace placeholders break i18next message in account UI
findings.body: `error-invalid-multivalued-size` was changed from `Attribute {{0}} must have at least {{1}} and at most {{2}} value(s).` to `Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.`. This file is consumed by the React/i18next based account console, where interpolation uses the double-brace syntax (see `backTo=Back to {{app}}` on line 3 and `error-invalid-length='{{0}}' must have a length between {{1}} and {{2}}.` on line 140). Single-brace placeholders are not interpolated by i18next, and `{2,choice,...}` is Java MessageFormat/ChoiceFormat syntax that i18next cannot evaluate, so the user will see the literal text `{0}`, `{1}` and `{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}` instead of the actual limits and pluralized word.

findings.title: Java ChoiceFormat syntax introduced into admin UI i18next bundle
findings.body: `error-invalid-multivalued-size` now uses `{0}`/`{1}`/`{2}` plus a Java ChoiceFormat expression `{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}`. The admin console translates these keys with i18next (double-brace interpolation, as used by the other `{{0}}`-style error keys in this bundle), which neither substitutes single-brace placeholders nor understands ChoiceFormat. The message will be rendered verbatim to administrators, including the raw choice expression.

findings.title: Lithuanian translation replaced with Italian text
findings.body: `totpStep1` was changed to `Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:` which is Italian, not Lithuanian. The same Italian sentence was also introduced into `themes/src/main/resources-community/theme/base/login/messages/messages_lt.properties` (`loginTotpStep1`). Lithuanian users will see an Italian instruction on the OTP setup pages; the previous Lithuanian wording should be kept (minus the hard-coded app links that this PR removes elsewhere).

findings.title: Simplified Chinese file given Traditional Chinese text
findings.body: `totpStep1` was set to `在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：`, which is Traditional Chinese (手機/應用程式) and belongs in `messages_zh_TW.properties`. This file is the zh_CN (Simplified) bundle; the text should read e.g. `在您的手机上安装以下应用之一：`.

findings.title: Malformed character class makes English-file path derivation match too much
findings.body: `replaceAll("_[a-zA-Z-_]*\\.properties", "_en.properties")` contains the class `[a-zA-Z-_]`, where the trailing `-_` is parsed by java.util.regex as the range 0x2D..0x5F. That range covers `-`, `.`, `/`, digits, `:` and all upper-case letters, so the pattern can match far beyond the file name: for an absolute path that contains an underscore in any parent directory (e.g. a CI workspace like `/build_dir/keycloak/themes/.../messages_de.properties`) the greedy match starts at that earlier underscore and the whole path segment chain is replaced, producing a bogus English path and an immediate build failure. Escape the dash (`[a-zA-Z_-]`) and/or derive the sibling file from `File#getName()` only.

findings.title: Missing English counterpart aborts the build with an opaque RuntimeException
findings.body: If the derived `_en.properties` file does not exist (community-only bundles, base `messages.properties` files whose name does not match the locale regex, or any path-derivation mistake), `verifySafeHtml` throws a raw `RuntimeException`. `verify()` only catches `IOException`, so this escapes the Mojo as an unhandled runtime exception instead of a `MojoExecutionException` or a collected verification message, giving maintainers a stack trace rather than an actionable error.

findings.title: Diff substring can throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException while reporting a violation
findings.body: The common-prefix (`start`) and common-suffix (`end`) counters are computed independently and can overlap when the sanitized string differs in length from the input (the sanitizer regularly adds characters, e.g. missing close tags). For example value="aba" and sanitized="abba" yields start=2 and end=2, so `value.substring(2, 3-2)` throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException. The verifier then crashes with an index error instead of reporting the illegal HTML it just detected. Clamp the indices so that `start + end <= min(value.length(), sanitized.length())`.

findings.title: Anchor-mismatch message does not identify the file or key
findings.body: The message `"Didn't find anchor tag " + matcher.group() + " in original string"` omits both the properties file and the message key, unlike the HTML violation message a few lines above which includes `key` and `file`. Since the plugin runs over hundreds of bundles, a contributor seeing only this line cannot tell which translation needs fixing.

findings.title: No test asserts that valid translations produce no findings
findings.body: All four tests only assert that a violation message is present. There is no test feeding a legitimate translation (e.g. a `_de` file containing the same `<b>`/`<a href="...">` markup as its `_en` counterpart, or a message with a `{n,choice,...}` pattern) and asserting the result list is empty. Without such a case, false positives introduced by the normalization logic (unescaping, `<!-- -->` stripping, choice-format whitelist) would go unnoticed and break the whole build.
